_note: Claims register — every load-bearing figure this site publishes, the source that carries it, and the exact string that must be present in that source. Checked daily by scripts/check-claims.py against the LIVE site and the LIVE sources, so it verifies what is published rather than what is in the tree. Not a changelog and not a style guide: an entry earns its place only if the site states something a reader could check. Written 2026-08-26 after a figure sat live for 14 days beside a citation that never contained it.

contract.role: Authority for what may be claimed about EISV and in what words.

stop-rule.role: Defines the single pre-registered outcome read and its kill criterion.

claims.site_says: beat a last-value persistence baseline on none of seven streams
must_contain: The per-agent reference does useful work
claims.why: The claim NAME is asserted next to the figure, not just the document. Pinning the document alone is exactly what let this figure be borrowed from claim 3 and published as claim 4.

must_contain: BENCHMARK FAIL for the cold-start reconstruction; UNIDENTIFIED for the warmed deployed EMA
claims.why: The page must not upgrade a reconstruction's benchmark failure into a verdict on the reference that actually runs.

must_contain: the question is unresolved, not negative
claims.why: If the contract ever re-opens or re-closes this, the page is stating the wrong status the same day.
Both the date and the existence of a written kill criterion are load-bearing; 'pre-registered' without one is just a plan.

claims.site_says: Zero of seven streams beat last-value persistence
must_contain: The per-agent reference does useful work
claims.why: The page states all three caveats the contract attaches, including the one about three of seven agents being the same Pi. If the contract ever drops a caveat, the page is carrying a claim its source no longer supports.

must_contain: the question is unresolved, not negative
claims.why: The page files this question under open rather than closed. If the contract re-closes it in either direction, the page's own section structure is wrong, not just its wording.

claims.site_says: At 101 independent bad clusters the minimum detectable lift
claims.why: The bound survives the cohort withdrawal because it is a power calculation, not a result. It is quoted as sensitivity evidence for an open question and must never drift back into standing for a verdict.

retired_phrasings.why: Attributed individuality-v2 leg C to outcome prediction. Lived on the page for 14 days because a correction written on 2026-08-12 stayed on an unmerged branch while _canonical/FACTS.md kept the wrong version, so a later session read FACTS.md and re-asserted it. This entry exists to make that specific re-assertion loud.

Written on the research-identity branch on 2026-08-11 and removed before that page first shipped, so it was never live. Guarded anyway: it is the branch's own overclaim about outcome prediction, and reviving that branch's copy is the most likely way it would reach the site.

not_mechanically_checked.why: Anchored to a frozen, citable publication rather than a moving document. Deliberately NOT re-derived: it is a snapshot with a citation, not a current measurement. Listed here so the gap in coverage is stated rather than inferred.

claims: production counters on the data plate
not_mechanically_checked.why: Already covered by the daily refresh from governance state, which is the same meter the public unitares README uses.
